ChangedDecoders: Code 128 FNC3 is accepted anywhere in code sets A/B and marks the entire result as reader configuration. Codeword 96 remains numeric data in code set C.

BarcodeDecoded.ReaderInitialization and Code128SymbolMetadata preserve the flag through module, image and common scanner results. Contents are exposed for inspection; the library does not apply reader settings.

SHIFT, FNC4, FNC2 rejection, stop and checksum checks remain intact. GS1 Composite rejects initialization symbols as ordinary data carriers. No production dependency, comparison hint, oracle or scoring change.
AttributionLimits: This follow-up records 208/267 correct positive images versus 207/267 in the previous pass. Previously correct images lost: none; gained: code128-1/7.png. Paired negative completion is [28, 29, 30, 30]/31 with the current binary and [28, 29, 30, 29]/31 with the previous qualified binary. All outcomes remain sensitive to shared-host contention and wall-clock budgets; no universal timeout or recognition advantage is established. The newly recovered Code 128 image contains FNC3 reader initialization; its exact contents are exposed with explicit configuration metadata. No recognition allowance, family hint, oracle or scoring changes. Additional default-format checks are contract diagnostics, not a representative accuracy survey or performance comparison. Supplemental PDF417 images are regression evidence informed by prior remediation, not an unseen holdout. The invalid GS1 AI (3922) oracle and undeclared QR character encoding policies remain unchanged in scoring. Stacked DataBar and Expanded Stacked multiple-symbol localization and arbitrary perspective remain unproved; MaxiCode image scanning is unsupported.

RegressionProof.Coverage: Independent initialization image through single/all pixel decoders and default/explicit unified scanning; FNC3 positions and sets A/B; numeric 96 in C; FNC4 state; SHIFT/FNC2 rejection; GS1 hints and Composite rejection; typed metadata propagation; Code 128 and Data Matrix ordinary/configuration pairs remain distinct while repeated same-state observations collapse.
